`sudodrift diff` used to exit 1 on any change, which is too noisy for CI and cron jobs where only serious findings matter. This release adds `--fail-on`.

What is new in 0.3.0

- `sudodrift diff --fail-on low|medium|high`. The output does not change: every change is still printed. The exit code is 1 only when at least one shown change is at that level or above, and 0 otherwise. Changes hidden by `--ignore` or `--min-severity` never count. An unknown level such as `--fail-on urgent` is an error and exits 2. Without the flag, exit codes are the same as before (0 no drift, 1 drift, 2 error).

Example:

    sudodrift diff base.json now.json --fail-on high

Install

    VER=v0.3.0; ARCH=amd64   # or arm64
    curl -fsSLO https://github.com/sudodrift/sudodrift/releases/download/$VER/sudodrift_${VER#v}_linux_$ARCH.tar.gz
    curl -fsSLO https://github.com/sudodrift/sudodrift/releases/download/$VER/SHA256SUMS
    sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS --ignore-missing
    tar xzf sudodrift_${VER#v}_linux_$ARCH.tar.gz
    sudo install -m 0755 sudodrift /usr/local/bin/

Or with Go: `go install github.com/sudodrift/sudodrift/cmd/sudodrift@latest`

The arm64 build was not run on arm64 hardware.

Closes #6 (first filed as #2)
